summary:
LUNARIS 3D
LUNARIS 3D is an interactive 3D space exploration game that teaches sustainable agriculture on the Moon. Players collect lunar rocks and ice, process resources into fertile soil, and grow plants in a space greenhouse.

Inspired by NASA's ISRU (In-Situ Resource Utilization) research, the game demonstrates how resources found on the Moon can support future human life.

Key Features:
- Soil Production: Transforming lunar rocks into fertile soil through a five-stage process.
- Space Greenhouse: Growing plants in a pressurized environment.
- Plant Cultivation: Producing food, oxygen, and biomass from crops such as lettuce, radishes, strawberries, and spirulina.
- Resource Exploration: Discovering lunar ice, rocks, and supplies.
- Equipment Upgrades: Improving tools, mobility, water, and oxygen systems.
- Survival: Managing hunger and oxygen levels.
Project Significance:

LUNARIS 3D makes space agriculture and sustainable living easier to understand through interactive gameplay. It introduces resource utilization, food production, and life-support systems relevant to NASA's Artemis program and future lunar missions.
details:
LUNARIS 3D: Lunar Regolith Soil Production & ISRU Space Farming

Project Summary
Establishing a long-term human presence on the Moon under NASA's Artemis program requires solving a critical logistical challenge: astronauts cannot continuously transport agricultural soil, water, and fresh food from Earth. LUNARIS 3D is an interactive 3D voxel game designed to teach players how lunar agriculture actually works while keeping the experience fun, exploratory, and rewarding. Exploring a procedurally generated lunar surface under 1/6 g gravity, players mine anorthosite rocks and polar crater ice, scavenge supplies from docked shuttles and abandoned spacecraft wrecks, and operate a 5-stage scientific soil-conversion pipeline inside a pressurized Artemis greenhouse dome to grow crops, produce oxygen, and sustain life support.

Purpose of the Game
The core purpose of LUNARIS 3D is to teach the science of lunar farming through fun, hands-on gameplay ("learning by playing"). Rather than presenting space agriculture as dry textbook theory or abstract charts, the game turns real NASA In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) science into an engaging 3D survival sandbox. Players discover firsthand why plants cannot grow in raw, sharp, water-repellent lunar dust—and experience every step required to transform sterile Moon rock into living, fertile soil while exploring wrecks, upgrading their gear, managing hunger and oxygen, and harvesting their own space crops inside an illuminated lunar greenhouse.

Scientific Foundations & NASA Open Resources Used
All soil engineering stages, crop behaviors, and resource loops in LUNARIS 3D are modeled after open NASA research and peer-reviewed space agriculture literature:

1.     NASA Kennedy Space Center (KSC) IRAD WILD Project & Tabuchi et al. (2023):
Raw lunar regolith consists of sharp, abrasive mineral dust (40–100 micrometers) with no organic matter and strong water repellency (hydrophobicity). The simulator's Stage 1 (Physical Crushing & Milling) and Stage 2 (Porosity & Aeration Amendment using Biochar and Hydrogel) teach how mechanical milling and porous carbon additives break water repellency and enable root aeration.

2.     Apollo 11, 12, and 17 Real Regolith Plant Experiments (Paul & Ferl, 2022):
Laboratory experiments with genuine Apollo lunar samples demonstrated that plants face severe ionic stress and poor nutrient availability in raw regolith. Stage 3 (Microbiome & Bio-Remediation) teaches how inoculation with Bacillus bacteria and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) bio-solubilizes locked phosphorus and potassium into plant-available nutrients.

3.     Wamelink (2024) & Frontiers in Space Sciences (2026) — Artemis Closed-Loop Nutrition:
Stage 4 (Struvite & Organic Nutrient Cycle) demonstrates how closed-loop habitats recycle nitrogen, phosphorus, and carbon (N-P-C) by blending urine-recovered struvite (MgNH4PO4) and organic compost into remediated regolith to produce Fertile Lunar Soil.

4.     Shackleton Crater & Polar Water-Ice Extraction (Auxiliary ISRU):
Permanently shadowed lunar crater rims preserve accessible water-ice deposits. Stage 5 (Lunar Crater Ice Extractor) lets players mine crater ice from high terrain rims or spacecraft wreckage and melt it into clean irrigation water and recovered mineral biochar.

Complete Game Features & Mechanics

1.     5-Stage ISRU Soil Laboratory:
Inside the greenhouse dome, clicking the ISRU Crusher & Reactor opens the 5-stage scientific pipeline:

· Stage 1: Mill 1 Lunar Rock (Anorthosite/Basalt) into 2 Raw Regolith fines.

· Stage 2: Amend 2 Raw Regolith with 1 Biochar into 2 Porous Bio-Regolith (+Soil Index).

· Stage 3: Bio-remediate 2 Porous Bio-Regolith with microbes into 2 Fertile Lunar Soil (+Soil Index).

· Stage 4: Enrich soil with Struvite and organic nutrients for Fertile Lunar Soil (+Biomass and +Soil Index).

· Stage 5: Melt 1 Lunar Crater Ice to completely refill the Watering Can and recover 1 Biochar.

1.     Pressurized Artemis Greenhouse Dome:
Built with Habitat Dome Glass, structural rock corners, interactive Airlock Doors, an ISRU Crusher & Reactor, a Water Reservoir for refilling water cans, and an interactive ceiling-mounted Greenhouse Grow Lamp that illuminates the interior and can be toggled on or off.

2.     Space Crops & Closed-Loop Farming:
Seeds must be planted directly onto Fertile Lunar Soil and actively watered (F key) to grow. Mature crops yield a 3x harvest and replenish vital telemetry:

· Artemis Lettuce (Lactuca): 40s growth, +25% Hunger, +1 Heart, +1.8 kg Biomass, +2% O2.

· Hydro-Radish: 24s fast growth, +20% Hunger, +1 Heart, +2.2 kg Biomass, +2% O2.

· Astro-Strawberry: 48s growth, +38% Hunger, +2 Hearts, +3.0 kg Biomass, +3% O2.

· O2 Spirulina Algae: 30s growth, +14% Hunger, +1 Heart, +2.6 kg Biomass, +6% O2, plus +1 bonus Biochar on harvest.

1.     Infinite Chunked Lunar Surface, Spacecraft Wrecks & Supply Chests:
The lunar world streams deterministically in 12x12 block chunks up to 240 blocks in every direction. A live Greenhouse Compass at the top of the screen continuously points toward the dome airlock and displays distance in meters. Near the base sits an intact docked Artemis Shuttle, while distant lunar sectors occasionally contain abandoned crashed spacecraft wrecks built from Titanium Hull, Solar Arrays, Fusion Beacons, Lunar Crater Ice, Cargo Crates, and interactive 15-slot Spaceship Supply Chests.

2.     Special Waters & Suit/Tool Upgrades (From Supply Chests):

· Special Waters: Purified Cryo-Water (full watering can refill +1 Heart), Nutrient Bio-Water (waters and boosts all planted crops by +50% growth and +4% Soil Index), and Deuterium Electro-Water (overcharges watering can +6 above max capacity, +5% O2, +20% Hunger).

· Suit & Tool Upgrades (up to Level 3): Laser Drill Chip (+35% mining speed per level), Exo-Servo Boots (+20% walk and sprint speed per level), Hydro-Tank Expander (+4 max watering can capacity per level), and Bio-Scrubber Core (+5% O2 and 20% slower hunger drain per level).

1.     Inventory, Sprint, and Multi-World Persistence:

· Minecraft-Style Inventory (Tab): 8 main hotbar slots (keys 1-8 or scroll wheel) and 27 backpack storage slots with drag-and-drop, right-click stack splitting, Shift+Click quick transfer, and a dedicated upgrade/water installation pad.

· Multi-World Game Menu (Z key): Create new worlds with custom names and seeds (generating distinct lunar terrain, craters, wrecks, and chest loot), automatically save progress to browser localStorage, and re-enter or delete previously saved worlds.

· Cross-Device Controls: Full Desktop support (Pointer Lock mouse look, WASD movement, double-tap W to sprint, Space for 1/6 g jump, Left/Right click to mine/place/interact, E to eat, F to water, Tab for inventory, Z for worlds/exit menu, H for guide) and Mobile Touch controls (virtual D-pad, 360-degree touch-look zone, and action buttons).

Open-Source Technology Stack

· Three.js (r160, MIT License): WebGL 3D voxel engine, InstancedMesh chunk optimization, directional shadow mapping, dynamic skybox with starfield and Earth, and procedural 64x64 HTML5 Canvas textures.

· Web Audio API: Real-time procedural sound synthesis for mining, block placement, lunar jumping, grinding, and crafting feedback with zero external audio files.

· Vanilla HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript & Google Fonts (EB Garamond, Plus Jakarta Sans, JetBrains Mono): Single-file, client-side architecture requiring no backend server or installation.

Use of AI Tools & Development Workflow Disclosure
In accordance with NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines, the following AI tools were used strictly as research, prototyping, and engineering assistants during development (the live game itself runs 100% client-side with zero runtime AI dependencies):

· Google NotebookLM: Used to organize, summarize, and cross-reference NASA open research documents, Apollo regolith studies, and space-agriculture scientific papers.

· Anthropic Claude: Used for initial scientific concept structuring, educational workflow design, and early simulation prototyping.

· Google Gemini & Google AI Studio: Used within Google AI Studio Build for interactive software engineering, expanding the Three.js chunk streaming engine, designing the greenhouse lighting, compass, Minecraft-style inventory, supply chests, suit upgrades, multi-world persistence, and web deployment.
